unit.why: A single narrative about the young rebbe of Mogielnica (grandson of the Kozienice Maggid) travelling to his master in Medzhybizh, a wealthy man who treats him coldly, the man's fall, his rescue through a nobleman, and the later recognition and explanation.

stories.start_quote: פ״א בימי ילדותו היה נסע למעזבוז
stories.end_quote: לכן ניחם ה׳ על הרעה לעשות טוב עמך
stories.summary_en: As a young man travelling to the Ohev Yisrael in Medzhybizh, the future rebbe of Mogielnica is seated by a rich man in the freezing cold beside the coachman, then warmed and asked for a word; he says 'cast your bread on the waters — even to a gentile', which leads the rich man to rescue a stuck nobleman; after the rich man falls into poverty, the nobleman, now a general, restores his fortune with an army supply contract; years later the man visits Mogielnica with Meir Shachna, recognizes the rebbe, and learns that his poverty was punishment for leaving the rebbe in the cold, shortened because he later warmed him.
